case_title: State of Haryana v. Mohd. Yunus & Ors.
accused_victim_relationship: Prior enmity/dispute (a fight the day before, per prosecution; previous enmity recorded in trial court judgment)
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.323, s.325, each read with s.34 (s.302/34 and s.323/34 were in issue on appeal)
evidence_type: Eyewitness (PW1, PW2, later disbelieved in part), medical evidence, recovery of weapons (recovery not proved against A1 and A2)
aggravating_circumstances: Multiple injuries to the victim's head; attack by several armed persons; weapons used
trial_court_outcome: Convicted A1-A3 under ss.302 and 323 r/w s.34 IPC; acquitted under s.325 r/w s.34; sentence not stated. A4 tried separately and acquitted on 05.10.2004
high_court_outcome: A1: acquitted of s.302/34, s.323/34 conviction maintained and sentenced to period already undergone. A2: appeal dismissed, conviction upheld. A3: appeal dismissed. Complainant's revision against A4's acquittal dismissed
offence_finally_established: IPC s.323 read with s.34 (hurt), for Mohd. Jamil (A2); Mohd. Yunus (A1) also stands convicted only under s.323 IPC
neutral_facts: On an evening in January 1999, the victim's brother (the informant) and the informant's son were sitting together warming themselves by a fire when the victim was about to walk home. Three men came to the spot to confront the victim over a fight that had broken out between them the previous day. One man carried a pharsa, another a kulhari and the third a lathi. According to the informant's first information report, one attacker struck the victim on the head with a pharsa and another struck him with the same weapon. A third blow was struck with a kulhari. When the victim fell, the lathi-carrying man struck his legs, and a further pharsa blow was delivered to his head. A person who tried to rescue the victim was struck on the shoulder with a lathi. The victim died about two days later from his injuries. A medical examination recorded four incised wounds to the scalp, and the rescuer had two blunt injuries. Police arrested the accused in stages. A lathi was recovered from one accused and a kulhari from another, and a blood-stained pharsa was recovered from a third. The fourth named person had no recovery made against him. The informant and the injured rescuer gave eyewitness accounts of the attack.
physical_harm: Death of the victim on 11.01.1999 from four incised head wounds; the rescuer (PW-2) had two blunt injuries to right shoulder and right hip joint
number_of_offences: 3 charged (ss.302, 323, 325, each r/w s.34); 1 finally upheld (s.323 r/w s.34 for Mohd. Jamil), with s.323 r/w s.34 also standing for Mohd. Yunus
premeditation_planning: Not stated. The court made no finding; the prosecution alleged the attackers came to teach a lesson after a fight the previous day
motive: Previous enmity between the parties (accepted by the court, para 18); alleged: to teach a lesson over a fight the day before
key_evidence_accepted: Court accepted the High Court's rejection of the FIR delay/ante-timing argument and found the recoveries of the kulhari and lathi unproved; it did not rely on the eyewitness evidence to convict the accused under s.302
witness_credibility: Eyewitnesses Deenu and Ahmad disbelieved in the second trial for contradictory statements, twisted facts and improvements; no reliance without strong corroboration
custody_duration: More than six months (per custody certificate) for Mohd. Jamil (A2)
bail_history: Mohd. Jamil (A2) was on bail during the pendency of the appeal
trial_duration: offence: 09.01.1999; trial judgment: 25.07.2001 (first trial; separate trial of A4 decided 05.10.2004); High Court: 26.10.2009; Supreme Court: 12 January 2024
legal_representation: Not stated individually; listed counsel appear 'for the appearing parties' without allocation to accused or State
investigation_status: FIR registered; arrests and recoveries made; charge sheet against A4 filed 01.04.2003; trial completed
procedural_irregularity: Witness statements recorded in two separate trials with contradictions between them; A4 separately tried after summons under s.319 Cr.P.C.
appeal_history: Trial court: A1-A3 convicted (ss.302 and 323 r/w s.34). High Court: A1 acquitted of s.302/34 and convicted under s.323/34; A2 and A3 appeals dismissed. Supreme Court: A2's s.302/34 conviction set aside, s.323/34 upheld; State's appeal against A1's acquittal dismissed
prosecution_argument: A2's conviction under s.302 r/w s.34 is supported by unimpeachable evidence; the same evidence should have been used to uphold A1's conviction under s.302 r/w s.34
defence_argument: FIR was ante-timed and delayed; witnesses were interested relatives; independent witnesses not examined; omissions and contradictions in witness statements; clothes not bloodstained
legal_principle_applied: For a s.302 trial, a witness branded untrustworthy for twisting facts and making contrary statements cannot safely support conviction; an eyewitness whose evidence is used to falsely implicate one accused cannot be relied on without strong corroboration
sentencing_rationale: Conviction under s.323 r/w s.34 not interfered with on the evidence; sentence already served, per custody certificate, exceeds the six months imposed
other_sentence_order: Bail bonds of Mohd. Jamil (A2) discharged
